correctness.rationale: For every pair of seven-bit words, deletion and at-most-once adjacent-transposition output-set intersection exactly characterizes ambiguous decoding. Python independently constructs all 128 output sets and exhaustive compatibility-graph cliques with provably valid greedy coloring bounds, obtaining optimum 16 and 28 labeled maximizing sets. Distinct C++ bitmask code exhaustively establishes zero deletion-only 17-cliques, 408 deletion-only 16-cliques, and precisely 28 of these also satisfying the transposition constraint. All eight reversal/complement representatives and their orbit sizes are independently reconstructed. Both programs were executed successfully using their actual packaged source paths; the proof is finite, no extrapolation.

value.rationale: Exact equality structure at the natural binary length 7 establishes 28 robust mixed-channel optimum designs, just 28 of 408 deletion-optimal choices, with eight sharp symmetry classes. All eight standard VT length-seven optimum-size syndrome classes fail the transposition condition, but the original deletion-correction size 16 is nevertheless retained. This distinguishes numerical capacity from the constructive solution landscape in a practical synchronization-error model; it is more than a textbook deduction or arbitrary unmotivated finite slice.
